title: Blue Stinger
subtitle: Stranded on Dinosaur Island
summary: Blue Stinger is Climax Graphics' action adventure, first released for Dreamcast in Japan on 25 March 1999.
body: Blue Stinger is Climax Graphics' action adventure, first released for Dreamcast in Japan on 25 March 1999. Emergency rescuer Eliot Ballade becomes stranded on Dinosaur Island, where monsters have overrun the complex. Working with other survivors and the mysterious Nephilim, he searches for a way through the island and the cause of the disaster. Exploration opens new areas through found items, while a variety of weapons supports the fighting. Producer Shinya Nishigaki conceived the project as a tribute to Western action films, giving its strange crisis the shape of an escalating rescue adventure.

The player can control Eliot or Dogs Bower while exploring the island's three-dimensional environments. Weapons and other supplies can be found or purchased, connecting combat to the resources gathered along the route. Optional missions offer further equipment, giving a detour a practical reward before the next dangerous area. Moving through the complex requires both defeating its inhabitants and finding the items that open another section. The relationship between shopping, exploration and fighting gives the disaster an unusual everyday detail: supplies remain useful commodities even while the surrounding island has become hostile.

The Japanese edition uses fixed camera positions, while the Western version follows behind the character and adds an optional first-person view. The change affects how the player reads the same spaces and approaches their threats. Monster designer Robert Short and storyboard artist Pete von Sholly were among the American contributors, while Toshihiko Sahashi composed the music. Blue Stinger accompanied Dreamcast's Western launch, presenting the new machine through a substantial three-dimensional adventure. Its mixture of colourful supplies, grotesque creatures and cinematic staging gave that early showcase a personality of its own.
story_headings: A changing view of the action
